extraction.name: Video-MME
extraction.description: A comprehensive multi-modal evaluation benchmark for multimodal large language models in video analysis. It includes 900 videos and 2,700 multiple-choice questions spanning diverse video domains, durations, and modalities such as subtitles and audio.
extraction.creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by collecting raw videos from YouTube across a domain hierarchy, then annotating them with multiple-choice question-answer pairs and performing a manual quality review.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw videos sourced from YouTube, including subtitles (if provided) and audios; 900 videos total.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning were recruited. Each annotator thoroughly viewed the entire video and iteratively created three relevant multiple-choice questions, each with four candidate options, for a total of 2,700 QA pairs. A separate manual review step checked that the language was clear and precise, the question was answerable with logically consistent options, and the designated correct answer was appropriate; questions answerable from text alone were returned to the original annotator for revision.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality was assessed through a manual review by a different annotator and an additional text-only validation using Gemini 1.5 Pro to filter out questions that could be answered without video content. The paper reports that Gemini 1.5 Pro achieved less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: One QA pair per annotator creation, with each QA pair reviewed by a different annotator; each annotator created three questions per video.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators had strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini 1.5 Pro was used to evaluate text-only questions and filter out QA pairs that could be answered without video content.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes a long-tailed distribution in datasets for complex temporal understanding, which can pose acquisition challenges and may reflect imbalance in available training data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The evaluation highlights that performance declines as video duration increases, and that open-source models are constrained by restricted input frames, creating an information bottleneck for understanding long videos.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper suggests that improving long-context modeling and building datasets for complex temporal understanding will help MLLMs better understand long sequential world dynamics and support more robust temporal reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The discussed datasets are intended for instruction tuning and training MLLMs for temporal reasoning and robust temporal understanding in videos.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Randomly sample 3 videos from each class for certificate length analysis; filter out QA pairs that can be answered solely based on the textual questions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Collect raw videos from YouTube across a domain-tag hierarchy; obtain subtitles and audios when available; annotate videos with multiple-choice QA pairs; conduct manual quality review for clarity, logical consistency, and answerability; revise questions that do not meet criteria.
